DRAFT sample. Pre-matrimonial verification checks whether the main facts in a biodata are true. That usually means identity, education, work, marital status and family details. It does not judge character, and it should always happen with consent.

:::composite
A family in Pune likes a match from a marriage bureau. The biodata says the boy works at a large IT company. Before the roka, they ask politely for his offer letter and recent salary slips, and the boy's side shares them the same week.
:::

## What gets checked first?

Identity comes first. Families ask for a government ID with the number masked, or share documents through DigiLocker. Nobody should collect or store a full Aadhaar number.

### Education and work

Ask for degree certificates, the offer letter and recent salary slips. Then check that the company name matches across all of them.

:::experience

## How do you ask without offending anyone?

Ask both sides to share the same documents. When the request goes both ways, it reads as care, not suspicion.

:::msp-cta{placement="mid"}
:::

## What verification cannot tell you

Documents show facts, not temperament. A clean report does not promise a happy marriage, so spend time together as families as well.

If you suspect fraud, report it on the [National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal](https://cybercrime.gov.in/) or call the helpline on 1930.
